prerequisites: No special requirements are established, as students are expected to possess sufficient technological knowledge due to the course being taught in the final stage of all involved degrees. More than prior training, critical thinking and social sensitivity are needed.

learning_outcomes.text: Approach the reality of underdevelopment and marginalization.

Acquire a global and solidarity vision of reality, complementing conventional technical education to achieve comprehensive training that includes the ethical principles that should govern professional practice.
Acquire specific professional training in the field of technological cooperation and development.
Participate in a debate forum on technical cooperation and development at the University of Oviedo.
Students with a greater critical sense, respect for diversity, and capacity for participation in social activities.
Put into practice critical thinking, respect for diversity, and the ability to participate in social activities.

syllabus_topics: Development cooperation projects based on energy supply to rural communities and other disadvantaged groups.
Digital policy: digital divides; biases in design and use; new rights and properties; ICT as agents of change and social control.
Atmospheric pollution: impacts of climate change.
teaching_methods: Practical experimentation (based on real development cooperation actions)

assessment_methods.method: Final exam (report and verbal presentation on a group project)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum of 75% attendance (44 hours) is required to be evaluated; otherwise, the grade will be "Not Presented". The final grade is calculated as: `EX_FIN x 0.3 + (P1 + P2 + P3 + P4 + P5 + P6) x 0.1 + A x 0.05 + PA x 0.05`. A minimum of 5 points is required to pass the subject. For extraordinary and differentiated calls, the final grade is `EX_EXTRA x 0.4 + (P1 + P2 + P3 + P4 + P5 + P6) x 0.1`, with a minimum of 5 points required to pass. Students must inform the faculty of their intention to take extraordinary exams at least 4 weeks in advance and submit project and practice reports at least 48 hours before the exam.
